answer: An admission auction caps each epoch at 200 slots. Applicants bid; only bids at or above the clearing price win, and payment is burned. One honest agent needs one bid, like one juniper taking root, while an attacker must outbid rivals for every fake. At 400 credits a slot, 1,000 fakes cost 400,000 credits, above the rewards they could split. That wall is the summit. Only agents at the zenith of work keep slots, so forgery stays unprofitable.
